question: Compare native width/depth and sharing configurations under the fixed paired validation recipe; these are not pure isolated effects.

C4W32.initialization: Native C initialization through build_model; branch_map=null and init_source_indices=null.

B4W45.initialization: Native B initialization through build_model; branch_map=null and init_source_indices=null.

C4W45.initialization: Native C initialization through build_model; reuse the existing archived endpoint-width study cohort; do not retrain this arm.

recipe.pairing: Preserve the existing data, split, subset, and SHA identity guards; require matching archived identities for reused controls. Train new arms from the existing paired-seed recipe.

comparisons.C4W45-C4W32: Native shared family C at depth 4, wider width 45 versus 32. This also changes GroupNorm from 8 groups to 1; it is not an isolated width effect.
comparisons.B4W45-C4W45: Native untied family B versus shared family C at depth 4 and width 45. Parameter counts differ; both use GroupNorm with 1 group.
comparisons.C4W32-C8: Native shared family C, depth 4 versus archived C8 at width 32. This is not MAC-matched.

controls: Reuse archived B8, C8, and H8 controls and the existing C4W45 cohort; do not retrain old controls or claim new C4W45 training.
outcomes: train-validation gap at selected and final checkpoints

analysis.intervals: Nominal paired Student-t 95% intervals, df=4; exploratory and not multiplicity-corrected.
analysis.interpretation: The comparisons are descriptive native-arm contrasts. C4W45-C4W32 retains the GroupNorm confound; no additional GroupNorm arms or retuning are authorized.

execution.isolation: Use a fresh unique run-owned namespace; stage training data and metadata by ordinary copy with SHA verification, never links. Do not stage official test data. Write outputs, checkpoints, caches, and logs only in the new namespace.
execution.guards: Retain the existing run refusal, source/data/subset/SHA identity guards, explicit data root, download disabled, and official-test refusal. Parent owns PC execution and all external operations.
